seo.meta_description: Adalbert: meaning “Noble and bright; noble and famous”, Germanic origin. Verified etymology, Biblical status and pronunciation.
seo.description_paragraph: Adalbert is a name of Germanic origin meaning “Noble and bright; noble and famous”. A Germanic compound of adal 'noble' and beraht 'bright, shining, famous' - 'noble and bright'. Its root is Old German adal 'noble' + beraht 'bright, shining, famous'. Adalbert is a Germanic name with documented Christian usage, not a Biblical name.

faq.q: What does the name Adalbert mean?
faq.a: Adalbert means “Noble and bright; noble and famous”.

faq.q: What is the origin of the name Adalbert?
faq.a: Adalbert is of Germanic origin.

faq.q: What language does the name Adalbert come from?
faq.a: Adalbert is used in Old German, English, Latin, Polish.

faq.q: Is Adalbert a boy's name or a girl's name?
faq.a: Adalbert is used as a male name.

faq.q: How is Adalbert pronounced?
faq.a: Adalbert is pronounced AD-əl-bərt.

faq.q: How is Adalbert written in Latin?
faq.a: Adalbert is written Adalbertus in Latin script.

faq.q: What is the linguistic root of Adalbert?
faq.a: The root of Adalbert is Old German adal 'noble' + beraht 'bright, shining, famous'.

faq.q: What is the etymology of Adalbert?
faq.a: A Germanic compound of adal 'noble' and beraht 'bright, shining, famous' - 'noble and bright'.

faq.q: Does Adalbert appear in the Bible?
faq.a: No. The name does not occur in the Bible. It has documented Christian historical usage through Saint Adalbert of Prague.

faq.q: Is Adalbert a Biblical name?
faq.a: No. Adalbert is not a Biblical personal name; it is of Germanic origin.

faq.q: Does Adalbert occur in the Old Testament?
faq.a: No — it is not attested in the Old Testament.

faq.q: Does Adalbert occur in the New Testament?
faq.a: No — it is not attested in the New Testament.

faq.q: Is Adalbert associated with a saint?
faq.a: Yes — Saint Adalbert of Prague (c. 956-997). Bishop of Prague and missionary, martyred in 997; venerated as a saint in the Catholic and Orthodox traditions.

faq.q: Is the meaning of Adalbert verified?
faq.a: The meaning “Noble and bright; noble and famous” is supported by Christian history: borne by Saint Adalbert of Prague (c. 956-997), bishop and martyr. Confidence: HIGH.

faq.q: What is the numerology or lucky number of Adalbert?
faq.a: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Adalbert total 63, reducing to 9. Number 9 is traditionally associated with compassion, idealism and completion. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What are the common spelling variants of Adalbert?
faq.a: Variants and alternative forms include Adalbertus, Wojciech (Polish equivalent), Albert (related).

faq.q: What is the transliteration of Adalbert?
faq.a: Adalbert is transliterated as Adalbert.

faq.q: How many syllables does Adalbert have?
faq.a: Adalbert has 3 syllables.

faq.q: What are the spiritual connotations of Adalbert?
faq.a: Any spiritual significance attached to Adalbert is interpretive. Its documented core is the lexical meaning “Noble and bright; noble and famous”, and readings built on that meaning are presented as tradition rather than as religious doctrine.

faq.q: Where is the name Adalbert used today?
faq.a: Adalbert circulates chiefly in Old German, English, Latin, Polish naming communities. No verified registration statistics are published for it.
